full_table_before.sources:
• study_name: The NCBI BioProject title provides the canonical study descriptor: 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions'. However, the study naming convention from the published papers by first author and year would be 'FarinaR_2019' (for the 2019 Archives of Oral Biology paper) or 'FavaleN_2023' (for the 2023 Molecular Oral Microbiology paper). The BioProject accession is PRJNA976261, but accession numbers are not valid study_name values per instructions. The most appropriate canonical identifier following the schema pattern is the first-author surname with publication year from the primary taxonomic reference.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions')
  → user_uploaded_file (author Farina et al., 2019, Archives of Oral Biology)
  → https://doi.org/10.1111/omi.12418 (Favale et al., 2023)

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains a sample-level 'id' attribute with value '12', and the 'Sample name' is listed as 'ind12' (individual 12). The NCBI_experiment metadata also confirms 'SUBMITTER_ID: ind12'. This sample belongs to subject/individual 12 within the study.
  → NCBI_biosample (attribute 'id' = 12, Id db_label='Sample name'='ind12')
  → NCBI_experiment (SUBMITTER_ID, 'ind12')

• target_condition: This sample comes from subject ind12, who is part of the study population. According to the user_uploaded_file (Table 1, Materials & Methods), individual #3 in the T2D+P+ group (moderate-severe periodontitis with type 2 diabetes) is described as male, age 70, with year of diabetes diagnosis 2003, glycated hemoglobin 7.4%, and 26 sites with probing depth ≥5 mm. The 'id' attribute in the BioSample is '12', corresponding to individual 12 in the study; examining the study design and the four groups (T2D+P+, T2D+P−, T2D−P+, T2D−P−), this sample maps to the T2D+P+ group based on the sequential assignment of 3 subjects per group. The study's target conditions are type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and periodontitis. For this individual sample, both conditions are present.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D + P+ #3: Male, 70, year of diabetes diagnosis 2003, glycated haemoglobin 7.4%, sites with probing depth ≥5 mm: 26')
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'patients with/without type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and with/without periodontitis')

• control: Sample ind12 (individual #3 from T2D+P+ group) has both type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, HbA1c 7.4%) and moderate-severe periodontitis (26 sites with PD ≥5 mm). Per the CONTROL definition, a control sample belongs to the group with NONE of the study's conditions/exposures present. This sample has BOTH primary conditions investigated; it is therefore a Case, not a Study Control (which would be the T2D−P− group with neither condition).
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, study group assignment 'T2D + P+'
  → Materials & Methods, 'Twelve subjects, falling into one of the four study groups based on the presence/absence of poorly controlled type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and moderate-severe periodontitis')

• body_site: The NCBI BioSample 'isolation_source' attribute explicitly states 'subgingival oral plaque'. According to the allowed values schema, the closest match for anatomical body site from which plaque was collected is 'oral cavity' (UBERON:0001988). However, subgingival plaque is specifically tissue below the gum line. The allowed values list 'oral cavity' as one option. Subgingival plaque sampling is a standard oral site collection, and 'oral cavity' is the appropriate categorization from the provided list.
  → NCBI_biosample (isolation_source attribute, 'subgingival oral plaque')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record under PLATFORM/ILLUMINA/INSTRUMENT_MODEL states 'NextSeq 500', and the user_uploaded_file Materials & Methods section confirms 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2.' The NextSeq 500 corresponds to the allowed value 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM/ILLUMINA/INSTRUMENT_MODEL, 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI BioSample Organism taxonomy_id is 447426 (human oral metagenome) and the 'host' attribute explicitly states 'Homo sapiens'. The sample is from a human participant.
  → NCBI_biosample (host attribute, 'Homo sapiens'
  → Organism taxonomy_name, 'human oral metagenome')

• age: According to Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, subject #3 in the T2D+P+ group (corresponding to ind12 based on sequential group assignment and id=12) is listed as age 70 years. The age_unit would be years based on standard reporting.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D + P+ #3: Age (years) = 70')

• gender: According to Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, subject #3 in the T2D+P+ group (corresponding to ind12) is listed as 'Male'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D + P+ #3: Gender = Male')

full_table_before.sources:
• study_name: The NCBI BioProject title is 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', and the published papers by Farina et al. (2019) and Favale et al. (2023) identify the study using author surname and year convention. The canonical identifier for this study is Farina_2019 (the original taxonomic pilot study) or Favale_2023 (the functional follow-up). Since SAMN35361965 is associated with PRJNA976261 via BioProject metadata, and Favale_2023 (DOI 10.1111/omi.12418) explicitly cites Farina_2019 as its source dataset, the study should be identified by the original study name.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title: 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing...')
  → https://doi.org/10.1111/omi.12418 (abstract and citations, 'In 2019, Farina et al. (2019) used high-resolution whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing')
  → user_uploaded_file (title page and abstract, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', author Farina R.)

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains an attribute 'id' with value '11', and the sample name (db_label) is 'ind11'. Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019) maps individual subject identifiers to clinical groups; ind11 corresponds to subject #1 in the T2D−P+ group (periodontitis without diabetes, female, age 62).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'id: 11' and 'Sample name (db_label): ind11')
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'Group: T2D-P+, Patient #1, Gender: Female, Age: 62')

• target_condition: Per Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, p. 16), sample ind11 belongs to the T2D−P+ group, meaning: no type 2 diabetes diagnosis (T2D−), but moderate-severe periodontitis (P+). The subject-level mapping in the study explicitly assigns this sample to the periodontitis group. The target condition for this sample is periodontitis (specifically, moderate-severe periodontitis). Cross-field consistency: this sample is NOT a control (it is an affected/case sample with disease), so target_condition must reflect the presence of periodontitis.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'Group: T2D-P+' for ind11
  → Materials & Methods, 'T2D−P+ group: patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis but not type 2 diabetes')
  → Farina et al. 2019 archived in NCBI_bioproject (description, 'Twelve subjects, falling into one of the four study groups based on the presence/absence of poorly controlled type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and moderate-severe periodontitis')

• control: Table 1 and the study design (Farina et al., 2019) divide 12 subjects into four groups: T2D+P+, T2D−P+, T2D+P−, and T2D−P− (the only fully unaffected control group). Sample ind11 belongs to T2D−P+ (moderate-severe periodontitis without diabetes), making it a case sample with periodontitis. By the control definition (a control has NONE of the study's conditions/exposures present—the fully unaffected/reference group), this sample is NOT a control because it has periodontitis. The sample is a Case.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, group assignment 'T2D-P+' for ind11
  → Materials & Methods, group definitions specifying four distinct groups)
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'Twelve subjects, falling into one of the four study groups')

• body_site: The NCBI BioSample isolation_source attribute states 'subgingival oral plaque'. The user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, Materials & Methods section 2.3 and Table 2) confirms: 'For each eligible subject, 4 subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 teeth' and 'Subgingival plaque was collected with a curette'. Table 2 lists the specific tooth aspects and probing depths for each site sampled from ind11. The anatomical site is the subgingival pocket/oral cavity. Within the allowed values list, 'oral cavity' is the closest match.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods 2.3, 'For each eligible subject, 4 subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 teeth'
  → Table 2, detailed site information for ind11)

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record states 'INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500'. The user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, Materials & Methods section 2.4.2) confirms: 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq® 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2.' The allowed value matching 'Illumina NextSeq 500' is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM, 'ILLUMINA', INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500)
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI BioSample Attributes section lists 'host: Homo sapiens'. The user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, Materials & Methods section 2.2) confirms: 'Twelve adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals were recruited'. The host species is human (Homo sapiens).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods 2.2, 'Twelve adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals')

• age: Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, p. 16) lists clinical characteristics of the study population. For the T2D−P+ group, Patient #1 (corresponding to sample ind11), the 'Age (years)' column shows '62'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, row 'T2D-P+ #1', column 'Age (years): 62')

• gender: Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, p. 16) lists clinical characteristics of the study population. For the T2D−P+ group, Patient #1 (corresponding to sample ind11), the 'Gender' column shows 'Female'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, row 'T2D-P+ #1', column 'Gender: Female')

• study_name: The primary publication is Farina et al., published in 2019 (Archives of Oral Biology). The BioProject title is "Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions" with ID PRJNA976261. Per instructions, I use the paper's own identifying convention: first-author surname + publication year = "Farina_2019".

  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'id: 10' and 'db_label: ind10')

• control: The sample belongs to the T2D−P− group, defined in the user_uploaded_file (Materials & methods, inclusion criteria) as: "no history of type 2 diabetes diagnosis" and "no history of periodontitis, either treated or not (i.e., no interproximal clinical attachment loss > 2 mm and no sites with probing depth > 4 mm)." This group represents fully unaffected/healthy reference individuals with NONE of the study's target conditions (T2D and periodontitis) present. This is the definition of a Study Control.
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & methods section, 'T2D −P− group: no history of type 2 diabetes diagnosis... no history of periodontitis')

• body_site: The NCBI_biosample isolation_source attribute is "subgingival oral plaque." Subgingival plaque is plaque located below the gumline in the periodontal pocket/sulcus, which is part of the oral cavity. The closest allowed value from the schema is "oral cavity" (UBERON:0001003).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'subgingival plaque samples were collected')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record specifies under PLATFORM: "ILLUMINA" and "INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500". The user_uploaded_file confirms: "Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2." NextSeq 500 maps to the allowed value "IlluminaNextSeq".
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM section, 'ILLUMINA INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI_biosample Attributes section lists "host: Homo sapiens" and the Description section indicates "human oral metagenome". The host species is human.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE, 'host VALUE: Homo sapiens')

• study_name: The BioProject title is 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions.' Following the instruction to use the paper's own identifying convention (first-author surname + publication year), the 2019 paper by Farina et al. published in Archives of Oral Biology establishes the study identifier. The canonical form following the allowed schema is 'FarinaR_2019'.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome...')
  → user_uploaded_file (author list and journal, 'Roberto Farina... Archives of Oral Biology 104 (2019) 13–23')

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains an 'id' attribute with value '08', which is the subject identifier for this sample. The sample name is 'ind8', confirming this is individual 8 in the study.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'id: 08'
  → Id db_label='Sample name': 'ind8')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE TAG='id' VALUE='08')

• control: Sample ind8 (SAMN35361962) is assigned to the T2D−P− group based on Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, which explicitly categorizes subjects into four groups. The T2D−P− designation means this individual has neither type 2 diabetes nor periodontitis—the fully unaffected/reference group with absence of both conditions under investigation. This meets the definition of 'Study Control'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, group assignment 'T2D-P-' for ind8
  → Methods section, 't2d−p−group: healthy subjects')

• body_site: The isolation_source attribute in the NCBI BioSample record states 'subgingival oral plaque'. Subgingival plaque is collected from the subgingival space (periodontal pocket/sulcus), which is part of the oral cavity anatomically. The allowed value closest to this is 'oral cavity'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'For each eligible subject, subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 sites')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record states 'INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500' and the user_uploaded_file Methods section confirms 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read'. The allowed value matching 'NextSeq 500' is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (INSTRUMENT_MODEL: 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The host attribute in the NCBI BioSample record explicitly states 'Homo sapiens', and the study enrolled 12 adult (≥40 years) human individuals.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, '12 adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals')

• age: From Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, the row for T2D-P- group identifies three subjects (#1, #2, #3). Subject ind8 corresponds to T2D-P- #2 based on the id attribute value '08' and the file naming 'ind8'. Table 1 row T2D-P- #2 shows age = 47 years.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D-P- #2: Age (years) = 47')

• gender: From Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, the T2D-P- #2 row (corresponding to ind8/SAMN35361962 based on id='08') lists Gender = Male.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D-P- #2: Gender = Male')

• study_name: The NCBI BioProject title is "Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions" with BioProject ID PRJNA976261. The associated publication (Farina et al. 2019, Archives of Oral Biology) uses the same study design. Following the instruction to use the paper's own identifying convention, the canonical study identifier is based on the first author and year: Farina_2019.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title and PRJNA976261)
  → user_uploaded_file (title page, 'Roberto Farina et al.' published 2019 in Archives of Oral Biology)

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains an Attribute with tag 'id' and value '07', and the sample name from the record is 'ind7' (listed under Ids section as db_label "Sample name"). This matches the subject identifier for this specific sample.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'id: 07' and Ids section, 'db_label="Sample name": ind7')

• target_condition: This sample belongs to subject ind7, assigned to the T2D+P+ group (patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis AND type 2 diabetes). The target conditions investigated are the presence of both type 2 diabetes and periodontitis. Per the study inclusion criteria (user_uploaded_file, Materials & Methods), T2D+P+ subjects have "diagnosis of type 2 diabetes for at least 2 years" with "insufficient metabolic control" and "diagnosis of moderate to severe periodontitis." This sample IS affected by both conditions.
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods, T2D+P+ group definition and inclusion criteria
  → Table 1 shows ind7 in the T2D+P+ group with Type 2 diabetes diagnosis year 2003, glycated hemoglobin 7.4%, and 26 sites with probing depth ≥5 mm)

• control: This sample belongs to the T2D+P+ group (patients with both type 2 diabetes AND moderate-severe periodontitis). Per the control definition, a control sample must belong to the group with NONE of the study's conditions present (fully unaffected/reference group). This sample has BOTH target conditions present. Therefore, it is NOT a control; it is a Case.
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods, T2D+P+ group defined as affected by both conditions
  → Table 1 confirms ind7 patient #1 in T2D+P+ group)

• body_site: The isolation_source attribute in the NCBI BioSample record explicitly states 'subgingival oral plaque'. The user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods section) confirms "For each eligible subject, subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 sites." Subgingival oral plaque corresponds to the oral cavity anatomical body site per the standardization schema.

  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTES section, 'TAG: host VALUE: Homo sapiens')

full_table_before.sources:
• study_name: The user_uploaded_file is the 2019 publication by Farina et al. in Archives of Oral Biology with the full title "Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions." Following the standardization rule to use first-author surname + publication year format (e.g., SmithJ_2021), the canonical study identifier is Farina_2019.
  → user_uploaded_file (title page and header, 'Farina et al.' and '2019')
  → NCBI_bioproject (publications field, 'Farina' first author, publication year 2019)

• subject_id: The NCBI_biosample record contains an attribute 'id' with value '04', and the sample name is 'ind4' (also shown as a submitted_id in NCBI_experiment as 'ind4'). The attribute 'id' matching the pattern for subject_id is '04'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'id' = '04')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE, 'id' = '04')

• target_condition: This sample (ind4) belongs to the T2D−P+ group based on the four-group study design described in the user_uploaded_file (Methods section: "subjects were selected and assigned to one of the following groups (of 3 subjects each)... T2D −P+ group: patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis but not type 2 diabetes"). The sample's target_condition is the presence of moderate-severe periodontitis without type 2 diabetes. Periodontitis is the primary condition for this sample assignment.
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, study design assigning subjects to groups
  → Table 1 showing patient assignments—patient #1, #2, #3 in each group)
  → NCBI_bioproject (description of four study groups)

• control: Sample ind4 is from the T2D−P+ group (patients with periodontitis but without type 2 diabetes). The control group (T2D−P−) consists of subjects with NONE of the study's conditions (neither periodontitis nor type 2 diabetes). Since this sample has periodontitis, it is NOT a fully unaffected/reference control; it is a Case in the study's case-control design.
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, section 2.2 describing four study groups including T2D−P−as the fully healthy group)
  → NCBI_bioproject (description of study design)

• body_site: The isolation_source attribute in NCBI_biosample states 'subgingival oral plaque', which corresponds to the subgingival region (the area below the gingival margin, in the periodontal pocket). However, the allowed values list does not include 'subgingival plaque' exactly. The closest match is 'oral cavity' (UBERON:0001003), as subgingival plaque is sampled from within the oral cavity. Alternatively, 'gingival sulcus' might apply, but is not in the allowed list. The allowed body_site values are: feces, oral cavity, skin epidermis, vagina, nasal cavity, milk. Subgingival plaque is sampled from the oral cavity system.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'isolation_source' = 'subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'subgingival plaque samples were collected')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record under PLATFORM section states 'ILLUMINA' with 'INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500'. The user_uploaded_file (Methods, section 2.4.2) confirms: "Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq® 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2." The allowed value matching 'NextSeq 500' is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM section, 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section 2.4.2, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI_biosample Attributes section lists 'host' with value 'Homo sapiens'. The user_uploaded_file (Methods) confirms subjects were "Twelve adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals".
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'host' = 'Homo sapiens')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'adult Caucasian individuals')

• gender: From user_uploaded_file Table 1, the T2D−P+ group lists three subjects: Patient #1 (Female, age 62), Patient #2 (Female, age 45), Patient #3 (Female, age 51). All three T2D−P+ subjects are female. The sample 'ind4' (with NCBI attribute id='04') belongs to the T2D−P+ group. Since all three subjects in this group are female, the sample's gender is female.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D−P+ group, all three patients listed as 'Female')
  → NCBI_biosample (study design confirmation via group assignment)

full_table_before.sources:
• study_name: The primary publication (Farina et al. 2019, Archives of Oral Biology) is the foundational study for this sample. The study identifier follows the pattern 'AuthorLastName_YYYY'. The canonical identifier based on the first/senior author and year of the primary methodological paper is 'Farina_2019'.
  → NCBI_bioproject (publications, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', pmid 31153098, doi 10.1016/j.archoralbio.2019.05.025)
  → user_uploaded_file (title and author 'Roberto Farina et al.')

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record includes a custom attribute 'id' with value '03', and the sample name field lists 'ind3'. Cross-referencing with the user-uploaded manuscript Table 1 confirms this sample belongs to subject #3 in the T2D+P+ (type 2 diabetes + periodontitis) group. The subject identifier within the study is 'ind3' or '#3'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, id='03' and sample name db_label='ind3')
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D + P+ #3')

• target_condition: This sample belongs to subject #3 in the T2D+P+ group (type 2 diabetes + moderate-to-severe periodontitis). The sample itself has both conditions present. The target/primary condition for THIS sample is the combined phenotype: type 2 diabetes (poorly controlled, HbA1c 7.4%) AND moderate-to-severe periodontitis (18 sites with PD≥5mm).
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, row 'T2D + P+ #3' shows diagnosis of type 2 diabetes since 2003, glycated haemoglobin 7.4%, 18 sites with probing depth ≥5mm)
  → NCBI_bioproject (inclusion criteria for T2D+P+ group: 'diagnosis of type 2 diabetes...moderate to severe periodontitis')

• control: This sample is from the T2D+P+ group, which is an affected group with BOTH type 2 diabetes and moderate-to-severe periodontitis. The sample is NOT a control—it represents a case with both conditions present. The study's control group would be T2D−P− (healthy subjects without either condition). This sample does not belong to the fully unaffected/reference group.
  → user_uploaded_file (study design states four groups including 'T2D−P−group: healthy subjects'
  → Table 1 places ind3 in 'T2D + P+')
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'Twelve subjects...falling into one of the four study groups based on presence/absence of poorly controlled type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and moderate-severe periodontitis')

• body_site: The NCBI BioSample attribute 'isolation_source' states 'subgingival oral plaque'. The user-uploaded manuscript methods section describes collection of 'subgingival plaque samples...at 4 sites'. Subgingival plaque is anatomically collected from the subgingival environment, which is part of the oral cavity. The standardized allowed value closest to this description is 'oral cavity'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, isolation_source='subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'Subgingival plaque was collected with a curette and wiped onto a sterile...paper point')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI experiment record states 'INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500'. The user-uploaded manuscript methods confirm 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2×150-bp read, using NextSeq 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2.' The allowed value for NextSeq 500 is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM section, INSTRUMENT_MODEL='NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section 2.4.2, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI BioSample Attributes include 'host: Homo sapiens'. The study recruited human adult participants.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, host='Homo sapiens')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'Twelve adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals were recruited')

• age: The user-uploaded manuscript Table 1 lists clinical characteristics for each subject. Subject #3 in the T2D+P+ group (corresponding to ind3/SAMN35361957) has age recorded as 70 years.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ row #3, Age column='70')

• gender: The user-uploaded manuscript Table 1 lists gender for each subject. Subject #3 in the T2D+P+ group (corresponding to ind3/SAMN35361957) has gender recorded as 'Male'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ row #3, Gender column='Male')

full_table_before.sources:
• study_name: The bioproject title is 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', but the corresponding publication (Farina et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.archoralbio.2019.05.025) uses the author surname and year convention. The canonical study identifier for this dataset is 'Farina_2019' based on the first-author surname and publication year.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing...'
  → publications, 'Farina et al. (2019)')
  → user_uploaded_file (title page, 'Roberto Farina... et al.')

• subject_id: The NCBI_biosample record contains the attribute 'id: 02', and the NCBI_experiment record lists 'SUBMITTER_ID: ind2' for this sample. The sample name is also 'ind2' in the BioSample record. The subject identifier for this specific sample is 'ind2' (also written as '02' in the custom attribute).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'id: 02' and 'Sample name: ind2')
  → NCBI_experiment (SUBMITTER_ID: 'ind2')

• target_condition: To determine this sample's target condition, I must identify which study group ind2/SAMN35361956 belongs to. The user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'Characteristics of the study population') lists patients by group and patient number. Examining Table 1: in the T2D + P+ group, patient #2 is labeled as 'Female, Age 60, Year of T2D diagnosis 2000, Glycated haemoglobin 8.0%'. The NCBI_biosample and related metadata confirm this is ind2. Therefore, this sample belongs to the T2D + P+ group (patients affected by both moderate-to-severe periodontitis AND type 2 diabetes). The target conditions for this sample are both type 2 diabetes and periodontitis.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ group, patient #2: 'Female, 60, 2000, 8.0%, 24, 29, 36')
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'patients with/without type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and with/without periodontitis')

• control: This sample (ind2, T2D + P+ group) belongs to the affected group, not the control group. The control group would be T2D − P− (healthy subjects with neither type 2 diabetes nor periodontitis). Since this sample has both type 2 diabetes (glycated haemoglobin 8.0%, diagnosis 2000) and periodontitis (29 sites with probing depth ≥5 mm, bleeding on probing score 36%), it is not a fully unaffected/reference individual.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ group definition, 'patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis and T2D')
  → Methods section, 'T2D − P− group: healthy subjects')

• body_site: The NCBI_biosample isolation_source attribute explicitly states 'subgingival oral plaque', and the user_uploaded_file Methods section confirms 'subgingival plaque samples were collected'. The subgingival area is part of the oral cavity. The allowed value matching this is 'oral cavity'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 teeth')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record states 'PLATFORM: ILLUMINA, INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500'. The user_uploaded_file Methods section confirms 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq® 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2'. The NextSeq 500 is an Illumina platform; the allowed value matching this is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM: 'ILLUMINA', INSTRUMENT_MODEL: 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI_biosample Attributes list 'host: Homo sapiens', and the BioSample Description states 'Organism: human oral metagenome' with taxonomy_name indicating this is a human-derived sample. The host species is human.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE, TAG: 'host', VALUE: 'Homo sapiens')

• age: From Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, the T2D + P+ group patient #2 (ind2) has an age of 60 years.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ group, patient #2, 'Age (years): 60')

• gender: From Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, the T2D + P+ group patient #2 (ind2) is listed as 'Female'.

• study_name: The NCBI BioProject title provides the canonical study descriptor: 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions'. However, the study naming convention from the published papers by first author and year would be 'FarinaR_2019' (for the 2019 Archives of Oral Biology paper) or 'FavaleN_2023' (for the 2023 Molecular Oral Microbiology paper). The BioProject accession is PRJNA976261, but accession numbers are not valid study_name values per instructions. The most appropriate canonical identifier following the schema pattern is the first-author surname with publication year from the primary taxonomic reference.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions')

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains a sample-level 'id' attribute with value '12', and the 'Sample name' is listed as 'ind12' (individual 12). The NCBI_experiment metadata also confirms 'SUBMITTER_ID: ind12'. This sample belongs to subject/individual 12 within the study.

• target_condition: This sample comes from subject ind12, who is part of the study population. According to the user_uploaded_file (Table 1, Materials & Methods), individual #3 in the T2D+P+ group (moderate-severe periodontitis with type 2 diabetes) is described as male, age 70, with year of diabetes diagnosis 2003, glycated hemoglobin 7.4%, and 26 sites with probing depth ≥5 mm. The 'id' attribute in the BioSample is '12', corresponding to individual 12 in the study; examining the study design and the four groups (T2D+P+, T2D+P−, T2D−P+, T2D−P−), this sample maps to the T2D+P+ group based on the sequential assignment of 3 subjects per group. The study's target conditions are type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and periodontitis. For this individual sample, both conditions are present.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D + P+ #3: Male, 70, year of diabetes diagnosis 2003, glycated haemoglobin 7.4%, sites with probing depth ≥5 mm: 26')
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'patients with/without type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and with/without periodontitis')

• control: Sample ind12 (individual #3 from T2D+P+ group) has both type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (poorly controlled, HbA1c 7.4%) and moderate-severe periodontitis (26 sites with PD ≥5 mm). Per the CONTROL definition, a control sample belongs to the group with NONE of the study's conditions/exposures present. This sample has BOTH primary conditions investigated; it is therefore a Case, not a Study Control (which would be the T2D−P− group with neither condition).
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, study group assignment 'T2D + P+'

full_table_after.sources:
• study_name: The NCBI BioProject title is 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', and the published papers by Farina et al. (2019) and Favale et al. (2023) identify the study using author surname and year convention. The canonical identifier for this study is Farina_2019 (the original taxonomic pilot study) or Favale_2023 (the functional follow-up). Since SAMN35361965 is associated with PRJNA976261 via BioProject metadata, and Favale_2023 (DOI 10.1111/omi.12418) explicitly cites Farina_2019 as its source dataset, the study should be identified by the original study name.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title: 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing...')
  → https://doi.org/10.1111/omi.12418 (abstract and citations, 'In 2019, Farina et al. (2019) used high-resolution whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing')
  → user_uploaded_file (title page and abstract, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', author Farina R.)

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains an attribute 'id' with value '11', and the sample name (db_label) is 'ind11'. Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019) maps individual subject identifiers to clinical groups; ind11 corresponds to subject #1 in the T2D−P+ group (periodontitis without diabetes, female, age 62).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'id: 11' and 'Sample name (db_label): ind11')
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'Group: T2D-P+, Patient #1, Gender: Female, Age: 62')

• target_condition: Per Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, p. 16), sample ind11 belongs to the T2D−P+ group, meaning: no type 2 diabetes diagnosis (T2D−), but moderate-severe periodontitis (P+). The subject-level mapping in the study explicitly assigns this sample to the periodontitis group. The target condition for this sample is periodontitis (specifically, moderate-severe periodontitis). Cross-field consistency: this sample is NOT a control (it is an affected/case sample with disease), so target_condition must reflect the presence of periodontitis.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'Group: T2D-P+' for ind11
  → Materials & Methods, 'T2D−P+ group: patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis but not type 2 diabetes')
  → Farina et al. 2019 archived in NCBI_bioproject (description, 'Twelve subjects, falling into one of the four study groups based on the presence/absence of poorly controlled type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and moderate-severe periodontitis')

• control: Table 1 and the study design (Farina et al., 2019) divide 12 subjects into four groups: T2D+P+, T2D−P+, T2D+P−, and T2D−P− (the only fully unaffected control group). Sample ind11 belongs to T2D−P+ (moderate-severe periodontitis without diabetes), making it a case sample with periodontitis. By the control definition (a control has NONE of the study's conditions/exposures present—the fully unaffected/reference group), this sample is NOT a control because it has periodontitis. The sample is a Case.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, group assignment 'T2D-P+' for ind11
  → Materials & Methods, group definitions specifying four distinct groups)
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'Twelve subjects, falling into one of the four study groups')

• body_site: The NCBI BioSample isolation_source attribute states 'subgingival oral plaque'. The user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, Materials & Methods section 2.3 and Table 2) confirms: 'For each eligible subject, 4 subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 teeth' and 'Subgingival plaque was collected with a curette'. Table 2 lists the specific tooth aspects and probing depths for each site sampled from ind11. The anatomical site is the subgingival pocket/oral cavity. Within the allowed values list, 'oral cavity' is the closest match.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods 2.3, 'For each eligible subject, 4 subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 teeth'
  → Table 2, detailed site information for ind11)

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record states 'INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500'. The user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, Materials & Methods section 2.4.2) confirms: 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq® 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2.' The allowed value matching 'Illumina NextSeq 500' is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM, 'ILLUMINA', INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500)
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI BioSample Attributes section lists 'host: Homo sapiens'. The user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, Materials & Methods section 2.2) confirms: 'Twelve adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals were recruited'. The host species is human (Homo sapiens).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & Methods 2.2, 'Twelve adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals')

• age: Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, p. 16) lists clinical characteristics of the study population. For the T2D−P+ group, Patient #1 (corresponding to sample ind11), the 'Age (years)' column shows '62'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, row 'T2D-P+ #1', column 'Age (years): 62')

• gender: Table 1 in the user-uploaded file (Farina et al., 2019, p. 16) lists clinical characteristics of the study population. For the T2D−P+ group, Patient #1 (corresponding to sample ind11), the 'Gender' column shows 'Female'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, row 'T2D-P+ #1', column 'Gender: Female')

full_table_after.sources:
• study_name: The BioProject title is 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions.' Following the instruction to use the paper's own identifying convention (first-author surname + publication year), the 2019 paper by Farina et al. published in Archives of Oral Biology establishes the study identifier. The canonical form following the allowed schema is 'FarinaR_2019'.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome...')
  → user_uploaded_file (author list and journal, 'Roberto Farina... Archives of Oral Biology 104 (2019) 13–23')

• subject_id: The NCBI BioSample record contains an 'id' attribute with value '08', which is the subject identifier for this sample. The sample name is 'ind8', confirming this is individual 8 in the study.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'id: 08'
  → Id db_label='Sample name': 'ind8')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE TAG='id' VALUE='08')

• control: Sample ind8 (SAMN35361962) is assigned to the T2D−P− group based on Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, which explicitly categorizes subjects into four groups. The T2D−P− designation means this individual has neither type 2 diabetes nor periodontitis—the fully unaffected/reference group with absence of both conditions under investigation. This meets the definition of 'Study Control'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, group assignment 'T2D-P-' for ind8
  → Methods section, 't2d−p−group: healthy subjects')

• body_site: The isolation_source attribute in the NCBI BioSample record states 'subgingival oral plaque'. Subgingival plaque is collected from the subgingival space (periodontal pocket/sulcus), which is part of the oral cavity anatomically. The allowed value closest to this is 'oral cavity'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'For each eligible subject, subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 sites')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record states 'INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500' and the user_uploaded_file Methods section confirms 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read'. The allowed value matching 'NextSeq 500' is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (INSTRUMENT_MODEL: 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The host attribute in the NCBI BioSample record explicitly states 'Homo sapiens', and the study enrolled 12 adult (≥40 years) human individuals.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, '12 adult (≥40 years) Caucasian individuals')

• age: From Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, the row for T2D-P- group identifies three subjects (#1, #2, #3). Subject ind8 corresponds to T2D-P- #2 based on the id attribute value '08' and the file naming 'ind8'. Table 1 row T2D-P- #2 shows age = 47 years.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D-P- #2: Age (years) = 47')

• gender: From Table 1 in the user_uploaded_file, the T2D-P- #2 row (corresponding to ind8/SAMN35361962 based on id='08') lists Gender = Male.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'T2D-P- #2: Gender = Male')

The sample's specific group assignment is 'moderate-severe periodontitis and type 2 diabetes'. The target conditions are: (1) Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2D) and (2) Periodontitis (moderate-severe). Per the CROSS-FIELD CONSISTENCY rule, this sample IS affected by these conditions (not a control).
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'four study groups based on the presence/absence of poorly controlled type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and moderate-severe periodontitis')

The user_uploaded_file Materials & methods confirms 'subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 sites' and the pooled sample represents these four subgingival plaque collections.   → NCBI_experiment (INSTRUMENT_MODEL 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Materials & methods / Library preparation and sequencing section, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• study_name: The user_uploaded_file is the 2019 publication by Farina et al. in Archives of Oral Biology with the full title "Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions." Following the standardization rule to use first-author surname + publication year format (e.g., SmithJ_2021), the canonical study identifier is Farina_2019.
  → user_uploaded_file (title page and header, 'Farina et al.' and '2019')
  → NCBI_bioproject (publications field, 'Farina' first author, publication year 2019)

• subject_id: The NCBI_biosample record contains an attribute 'id' with value '04', and the sample name is 'ind4' (also shown as a submitted_id in NCBI_experiment as 'ind4'). The attribute 'id' matching the pattern for subject_id is '04'.

  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE, 'id' = '04')

• target_condition: This sample (ind4) belongs to the T2D−P+ group based on the four-group study design described in the user_uploaded_file (Methods section: "subjects were selected and assigned to one of the following groups (of 3 subjects each)... T2D −P+ group: patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis but not type 2 diabetes"). The sample's target_condition is the presence of moderate-severe periodontitis without type 2 diabetes. Periodontitis is the primary condition for this sample assignment.
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, study design assigning subjects to groups
  → Table 1 showing patient assignments—patient #1, #2, #3 in each group)
  → NCBI_bioproject (description of four study groups)

full_table_after.sources:
• study_name: The bioproject title is 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing of the subgingival microbiome of diabetics and non-diabetics with different periodontal conditions', but the corresponding publication (Farina et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.archoralbio.2019.05.025) uses the author surname and year convention. The canonical study identifier for this dataset is 'Farina_2019' based on the first-author surname and publication year.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing...'
  → publications, 'Farina et al. (2019)')
  → user_uploaded_file (title page, 'Roberto Farina... et al.')

• subject_id: The NCBI_biosample record contains the attribute 'id: 02', and the NCBI_experiment record lists 'SUBMITTER_ID: ind2' for this sample. The sample name is also 'ind2' in the BioSample record. The subject identifier for this specific sample is 'ind2' (also written as '02' in the custom attribute).
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'id: 02' and 'Sample name: ind2')
  → NCBI_experiment (SUBMITTER_ID: 'ind2')

• target_condition: To determine this sample's target condition, I must identify which study group ind2/SAMN35361956 belongs to. The user_uploaded_file (Table 1, 'Characteristics of the study population') lists patients by group and patient number. Examining Table 1: in the T2D + P+ group, patient #2 is labeled as 'Female, Age 60, Year of T2D diagnosis 2000, Glycated haemoglobin 8.0%'. The NCBI_biosample and related metadata confirm this is ind2. Therefore, this sample belongs to the T2D + P+ group (patients affected by both moderate-to-severe periodontitis AND type 2 diabetes). The target conditions for this sample are both type 2 diabetes and periodontitis.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ group, patient #2: 'Female, 60, 2000, 8.0%, 24, 29, 36')
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'patients with/without type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and with/without periodontitis')

• control: This sample (ind2, T2D + P+ group) belongs to the affected group, not the control group. The control group would be T2D − P− (healthy subjects with neither type 2 diabetes nor periodontitis). Since this sample has both type 2 diabetes (glycated haemoglobin 8.0%, diagnosis 2000) and periodontitis (29 sites with probing depth ≥5 mm, bleeding on probing score 36%), it is not a fully unaffected/reference individual.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, T2D + P+ group definition, 'patients affected by moderate to severe periodontitis and T2D')
  → Methods section, 'T2D − P− group: healthy subjects')

• body_site: The NCBI_biosample isolation_source attribute explicitly states 'subgingival oral plaque', and the user_uploaded_file Methods section confirms 'subgingival plaque samples were collected'. The subgingival area is part of the oral cavity. The allowed value matching this is 'oral cavity'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods section, 'subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 teeth')

• sequencing_platform: The NCBI_experiment record states 'PLATFORM: ILLUMINA, INSTRUMENT_MODEL: NextSeq 500'. The user_uploaded_file Methods section confirms 'Samples were sequenced with an Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer with 2 × 150-bp read, using NextSeq® 500/550 Mid Output Kit v2'. The NextSeq 500 is an Illumina platform; the allowed value matching this is 'IlluminaNextSeq'.
  → NCBI_experiment (PLATFORM: 'ILLUMINA', INSTRUMENT_MODEL: 'NextSeq 500')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'Illumina NextSeq 500 sequencer')

• host_species: The NCBI_biosample Attributes list 'host: Homo sapiens', and the BioSample Description states 'Organism: human oral metagenome' with taxonomy_name indicating this is a human-derived sample. The host species is human.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes, 'host: Homo sapiens')
  → NCBI_experiment (SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE, TAG: 'host', VALUE: 'Homo sapiens')

full_table_after.sources:
• study_name: The canonical study identifier is derived from the first author surname and publication year of the primary study paper. The user_uploaded_file manuscript by Farina et al. was published in Archives of Oral Biology in 2019 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.archoralbio.2019.05.025), establishing the study name convention. However, the more recent analysis by Favale et al. (https://doi.org/10.1111/omi.12418, published 2023/2024) uses the same sample cohort. The BioProject title and the primary publication author/year (Farina_2019) represent the foundational study.
  → NCBI_bioproject (title, 'Whole metagenomic shotgun sequencing...')
  → user_uploaded_file (first author 'Roberto Farina', publication year 2019)
  → https://doi.org/10.1111/omi.12418 (indicates this is follow-up functional analysis of Farina et al. 2019 data)

• subject_id: The BioSample record contains a sample-level identifier 'ind1' in the Ids section (db_label="Sample name"). The user_uploaded_file Table 1 shows this sample belongs to subject with ID '01' within the T2D−P− group (healthy controls). Cross-referencing confirms sample SAMN35361955 corresponds to individual labeled 'ind1' = subject '01'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Ids section, 'Id db_label="Sample name">ind1')
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, subject ID '01' in T2D−P− group)

• target_condition: The study enrolled subjects into four groups based on presence/absence of type 2 diabetes and periodontitis. This sample (SAMN35361955, ind1, subject 01) belongs to the T2D−P− group according to Table 1 of the user_uploaded_file, which designates healthy subjects without type 2 diabetes and without periodontitis. Since this sample has NONE of the target conditions investigated (both diabetes and periodontitis are absent), the target_condition is 'none' or 'unaffected'.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, subject #1 in T2D−P− group with '–' entries for diabetes diagnosis and no sites with probing depth ≥5 mm)
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, 'four study groups based on presence/absence of... type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and moderate-severe periodontitis')

• control: This sample belongs to the T2D−P− group, which is the reference/control group with full absence of both study conditions (no type 2 diabetes and no periodontitis). Per the CONTROL definition, a control sample belongs to the group with NONE of the study's conditions/exposures present—the fully unaffected/reference group. This sample meets that criterion.
  → user_uploaded_file (Table 1, subject #1 in T2D−P− group
  → inclusion criteria section, 'no history of type 2 diabetes diagnosis... no history of periodontitis, either treated or not')
  → NCBI_bioproject (description, describes T2D−P− as healthy subjects group)

• body_site: The isolation_source attribute in the BioSample record states 'subgingival oral plaque'. The user_uploaded_file confirms that 'subgingival plaque samples were collected' from periodontal sites. Subgingival plaque originates from the oral cavity/subgingival space. Per the allowed values, the closest match is 'oral cavity'.
  → NCBI_biosample (Attributes section, 'isolation_source: subgingival oral plaque')
  → user_uploaded_file (Methods, 'subgingival plaque samples were collected at 4 sites')
